_comment: SHARED, PROJECT-NEUTRAL defaults for the machine-generated security count table. Numbers come from commitwork rollup.json via bin/build-security-data.mjs; only labels and State prose live in an annotations sidecar so they survive regeneration. {crit}/{high}/{med}/{low}/{kev}/{cves} tokens in State are filled from live counts. THIS FILE MUST STAY PROJECT-NEUTRAL: it is the fallback sidecar for EVERY project's rollup, so any editorial claim written here is asserted about whichever fleet is passed in. A project's own prose belongs in monitor/security-annotations.<report-dir>.json, which the generator selects automatically — see security-annotations.clientA-monorepo.json.
_history: Until 2026-08-03 this file held clientA's remediation history ('fully fixed (524 → 0)') and a clientA advisory id while serving as the default for any project. An audit reproduced the npm row rendering as `| npm / JavaScript | 0 | 13 | 0 | 0 | fully fixed (524 → 0) |` — a remediation verdict printed beside thirteen live highs, in the same table row. Rows may now declare an `asserts` block stating what their prose claims about the scan; when the scan disagrees the generator replaces the cell with the contradiction and exits 3. Every state string in THIS file is built from tokens alone, so it restates the counts and cannot go stale.
_toolSurfacesNote: A tool id here maps to a surface IF that tool appears in rollup.json repos[].findings. Measured against the scan of record on 2026-08-03, only `osv` did — the other eleven keys matched nothing. That is not a defect in the map (another area's scan may well carry npm-audit or gitleaks findings); it is the reason the map must not be read as a coverage claim. build-security-data.mjs now emits toolSurfaceCoverage {matched, declaredButUnseen, seenButUndeclared} into security-data.json and prints the unseen list, so a declared-but-absent surface reads as UNMEASURED rather than as a surface with zero findings. Note also that surfaceOrder covers npm+jvm only: sast and secrets are recognised here and counted, but not rendered in the table.
_notWired: bin/build-security-data.mjs is a MANUAL-RUN tool. No sweep, script, workflow or panel route invokes it, so this editorial layer does not regenerate on its own and any table it has injected is only as fresh as the last hand-run. Wiring it into the sweep (or into the panel's report generation) is unfinished work, recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered.
